overview: 110 official Qs (2008, 2017, 2019, 2025) – the heaviest Polity block. 40 are on Fundamental Rights alone (article numbers, writs, citizens-only rights, Emergency, property); then salient features/borrowed sources (16), Preamble (13), DPSP and constitutional development (11 each), Fundamental Duties (9). 75% are plain one-liners asking 'which Article / which Amendment / which year / which source'; 2025 added matching, assertion-reason and multi-statement formats.

possibility.what_they_ask: the concept behind a definition ('persons change, rules don't' = constitutional government); word origins (democracy – Greek).

possibility.angle: Constitutional development: British Acts and the Constituent Assembly
possibility.evidence: 11 Qs: 2017×5, 2019×3, 2025×3; very common in other APPSC exams (Regulating Act, 1858, 1909, 1919, 1935, CA committees)
possibility.what_they_ask: which Act introduced X (Governor-General of India, separate electorate, dyarchy, federation, budget discussion); CA dates (Drafting Committee 29 Aug 1947, adoption 26 Nov 1949, anthem 24 Jan 1950); committee chairmen; Indian Independence Act features.

possibility.angle: Salient features: borrowed sources, Parts/Schedules, citizenship, special provisions
possibility.what_they_ask: source country of a feature (judicial review – USA, Concurrent List – Australia, DPSP – Ireland, duties – USSR, residuary – Canada); Articles 5–11 = citizenship; original Schedules (8); Art 371A–371G states; books/remarks on the Constitution (D.D. Basu, Austin, H.V. Kamath).

exact word order (Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic); which words are in it (Justice social-economic-political, Liberty of thought-expression-belief-faith-worship); 42nd Amendment additions; source revolutions; Kesavananda (part of Constitution); 26 November.

possibility.angle: Fundamental Rights: articles, writs, scope, Emergency, property
possibility.what_they_ask: Article number for a quoted right (14, 17, 20, 21, 23, 25(1), 32, 33); writ meanings and scope; rights only for citizens; rights not suspendable (20, 21); 44th Amendment and Art 300A; Art 21 case law (privacy, right to die); 86th Amendment / Art 21A dates.
Article number for a directive (40 panchayats, 43 living wage, 45 early childhood, 46 weaker sections, 39(b)(c)); 'which is not a DPSP'; non-justiciability (Art 37).

possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs; leaf not yet asked
possibility.what_they_ask: natural targets: Champakam Dorairajan (1951), Golak Nath, Art 31C (25th/42nd Amd), Minerva Mills (1980, balance as basic structure); which DPSP was later made an FR (Art 45 → 21A).
Swaran Singh Committee; 42nd Amendment 1976; count (11); 11th duty by 86th Amd 2002; Art 51A / Part IVA; 'which is not a duty' (DPSP items planted).

possibility.angle: Amendment of the Constitution (Art 368, landmark amendments)
possibility.what_they_ask: Art 368; limits on amending power; what is not an Art 368 amendment (Arts 2–4); 42nd 'Mini-Constitution'; 97th Amendment (co-operatives, Part IXB, Art 43B).
which case made a feature basic (secularism – S.R. Bommai 1994); Kesavananda 1973 origin.

traps.spot: Options are adjacent amendment numbers or the same number with different years
traps.fix: 42nd (1976): Socialist, Secular, Integrity, Fundamental Duties. 44th (1978): property out of Part III, Arts 20–21 non-suspendable. 86th (2002): Art 21A, new Art 45, duty 51A(k).
traps.pyq: 'Right to Property was deleted by the ___ Amendment' → 44th, not 42nd [group2-2008-paper2#125]; '11th Fundamental Duty' → 86th Act 2002, not 96th / 2001 [mains-2025-paper1#108]

traps.spot: Stem says 'came into force' and options hold both 2002 and 2010
traps.fix: Art 21A inserted 2002 by the 86th Amendment, enforced 1 April 2010 with the RTE Act 2009.
traps.pyq: 'Right to education came into force as FR' → 2010 [prelims-2017#39] vs 'made primary education a FR in' → 2002 [group2-2008-paper2#122]

traps.trap: Plants a DPSP item as a Fundamental Right or Duty
traps.spot: 'Which is not a FR / not a duty' with a welfare-sounding option (work, weaker sections, elderly)
traps.fix: Work (Art 41), weaker sections (Art 46) are DPSP; duties are only the 11 in Art 51A.
traps.pyq: 'To protect the weaker sections from social injustice' as a duty → false, it is Art 46 [prelims-2019#60]; 'Right to work' → not a FR [mains-2019-paper2#139]

traps.trap: Moves a qualifier to the wrong Preamble ideal
traps.spot: Negative Q: 'not embodied in the Preamble' with Liberty/Justice combined with a qualifier
traps.fix: Justice → social, economic, political. Liberty → thought, expression, belief, faith, worship. 'Political liberty' and 'Freedom' are not in the text.
traps.pyq: 'Political Liberty' not in Preamble [mains-2025-paper1#123]; 'Freedom' not used [prelims-2019#52]

traps.trap: Shuffles word order of the Preamble's description of India
traps.spot: All four options contain the same five words
traps.fix: Order is S-S-S-D-R: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic.
traps.pyq: 'India is a ...' → Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic [prelims-2017#28]

traps.trap: Swaps the source country of a borrowed feature
traps.spot: Matching of countries vs features, or 'borrowed from'
traps.fix: UK – rule of law, single citizenship, parliamentary system; USA – judicial review, FRs; Ireland – DPSP; Canada – residuary with Centre; Australia – Concurrent List; Weimar Germany – suspension of FRs; USSR – duties; GoI Act 1935 – emergency, federal scheme.
traps.pyq: Emergency provisions → GoI Act 1935, suspension of FRs → Germany [mains-2025-paper1#78]; DPSP → Ireland, residual powers → Canada [mains-2025-paper1#125]

traps.trap: Swaps writs and their literal meanings / scope
traps.spot: Writ matching, or 'which writ lies against a private person'
traps.fix: Habeas corpus 'have the body' (also against private persons); Mandamus 'we command'; Certiorari 'to be certified'; Quo warranto 'by what authority'.
traps.pyq: Writ against private person → Habeas Corpus [prelims-2017#35]; Mandamus 'we command' [mains-2025-paper1#87]

traps.trap: Confuses citizens-only rights with rights for all persons
traps.spot: 'available only to citizens' or statements on aliens
traps.fix: Citizens only: Arts 15, 16, 19, 29, 30. All persons: 14, 20, 21, 25. Enemy aliens lose Art 22 safeguards.
traps.pyq: 'Only to a citizen' → Article 19 [prelims-2017#45]; 'no difference between friendly and enemy aliens' is the false statement [mains-2017-paper2#101]

traps.trap: Swaps adopted / enforced / anthem dates of the Constituent Assembly
traps.fix: Adopted 26 Nov 1949 (Constitution Day); in force 26 Jan 1950; anthem and President elected 24 Jan 1950.
traps.pyq: 'Adopted by the CA on' → 26 Nov 1949 [mains-2025-paper1#81]; anthem → 24 Jan 1950 [mains-2019-paper2#137]

traps.trap: Gives the right British Act the wrong reform
traps.spot: Matching of Acts with reforms, adjacent Council Acts (1861/1892/1909)
traps.fix: 1833 – GG of India; 1861 – portfolio, nominated Indians; 1892 – budget discussion; 1909 – separate electorate; 1919 – provincial dyarchy; 1935 – All-India Federation.
traps.pyq: Budget discussion → 1892 (not 1861); separate Muslim representation → 1909 [mains-2025-paper1#121]; GG of Bengal → GG of India by Charter Act 1833 [mains-2025-paper1#105]

techniques.name: Article-band locator [Part III / IV / IVA]
techniques.how: Place the quoted right in its band first: 14–18 equality, 19–22 freedom, 23–24 exploitation, 25–28 religion, 29–30 culture, 32 remedies, 36–51 DPSP, 51A duties. Only options inside the band survive.
techniques.example: 'Organise village panchayats' is a directive → 36–51 band → 73, 74, 64 fall → Article 40 [group2-2008-paper2#137]

techniques.name: Amendment-timeline anchor
techniques.how: Fix 1976 (42nd) – 1978 (44th) – 2002 (86th) – 2011 (97th). The content tells the era: additions to Preamble/duties = 1976; repairing Emergency excesses = 1978; education = 2002.
techniques.example: Environment duty added → it is a Fundamental Duty → all duties except (k) are 42nd/1976 → 1978, 1983, 2004 fall → 1976 [group2-2008-paper2#104]

techniques.name: Negative-question flip
techniques.how: In 'all correct except', test each option against the article text; the one that contradicts a stated safeguard is the answer. Mark T/F beside each before looking at the key.
techniques.example: Art 20(1) bars retrospective criminal law → 'Parliament can make criminal law with retrospective effect' is false → answer [mains-2017-paper2#108]

techniques.name: Matching: solve the sure pair first
techniques.how: Fix the pair you are certain of, strike options without it, then the second sure pair usually leaves one code.
techniques.example: Mandamus = 'we command' (b-iii) keeps only options 2 and 3; Quo warranto = 'by what authority' (a-ii) leaves a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i [mains-2025-paper1#87]

techniques.name: Text-recall for Preamble
techniques.how: Recite the Preamble line in your head and tick only words actually in it; qualifiers attach to one ideal only.
techniques.example: Recite 'LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship' → thought/belief/expression present → 'Political Liberty' absent [mains-2025-paper1#123]

techniques.name: Assertion-reason: test the 'because'
techniques.how: After A and R are both true, ask whether R is the legal cause of A. Constitutional text causes (e.g. Art 37, 44th Amd) beat descriptive roles.
techniques.example: Property is a legal right under 300A because the 44th Amd removed it from Part III → R explains A [mains-2025-paper1#133]; DPSP non-enforceable because Art 37 says so, not because they guide legislation → R not explanation [mains-2025-paper1#139]

confusions.remember: 32 = SC, only FRs, itself a FR; 226 = HC, FRs 'and for any other purpose' – wider.
137 = SC reviews its own judgment; 13 = laws inconsistent with FRs are void (judicial review, severability).
20 = conviction protections (ex post facto, double jeopardy, self-incrimination); 22 = arrest/detention safeguards, not for preventive detention or enemy aliens.
23 = trafficking, begar, forced labour; 24 = children below 14 in factories/mines.
21A = education 6–14 as a right; 45 now = early childhood care below 6.
40 village panchayats; 43 living wage, decent life, leisure; 46 educational-economic interests of SC/ST/weaker sections.
Social-economic-political justice from Russia 1917; the trio from France 1789.
Berubari: Preamble not part; Kesavananda: Preamble is part and basic structure limits amendment.
Kesavananda created basic structure; Bommai (9 judges) declared secularism a basic feature.
Swaran Singh recommended duties; Verma looked at operationalising them.
Sinha – temporary president of the first CA sitting (9 Dec 1946); Prasad – permanent President (11 Dec 1946).
Nehru – Union Powers, Union Constitution, States; Ambedkar – Drafting; Prasad – Rules of Procedure, Steering.
Austin – 'Cornerstone of a Nation', DPSP 'social revolution'; Basu – 'Introduction to the Constitution of India'.
A-Nagaland, B-Assam, C-Manipur, F-Sikkim, G-Mizoram, H-Arunachal, D/E-AP.
After 1978 property is enforced via Art 226 or civil suit, not Art 32.
Only habeas corpus lies against private persons; the rest target public bodies/offices.

anchors: Part III = Arts 12–35 (six groups of FRs; seven before 1978)
Part II Arts 5–11 = Citizenship; Art 11 – Parliament regulates citizenship
Art 17 untouchability, Art 18 titles – social equality
Arts 20 and 21 cannot be suspended in Emergency (44th Amd 1978)
Art 21 – privacy (Puttaswamy 2017); right to die excluded (Chenna Jagadeeswar 1988 AP HC; Gian Kaur 1996)
Art 32 – Ambedkar's 'heart and soul'; Art 33 – restrict FRs of armed forces
Art 37 – DPSPs not enforceable but fundamental in governance
Art 51A – 11 duties; 10 in 1976 (42nd), (k) in 2002 (86th); Part IVA
97th Amd 2011 – co-operatives: Art 19(1)(c), Art 43B, Part IXB
Art 368 – amending power; Arts 2–4 changes are not Art 368 amendments
29 Aug 1947 Drafting Committee; 26 Nov 1949 adoption; 24 Jan 1950 anthem; 26 Jan 1950 in force
Charter Act 1833 – GG of India; 1909 separate electorate; 1919 dyarchy; 1935 federation
checklist: Which band does the quoted right/directive belong to (FR 12–35, DPSP 36–51, duty 51A)?
Is the stem asking insertion year or coming-into-force year?
Amendment options: which of 42 / 44 / 86 matches the content's era?
Negative stem? Mark each option T/F against the article text before choosing.
Preamble: recite the exact line; check which ideal the qualifier belongs to.
Matching: lock one certain pair, strike codes, then a second pair.
Assertion-reason: is R the legal cause of A or just another true fact?
